source.verification_required: Captured in-task for Lane A item A-02a by one direct GET of the official DCP Zoning Resolution portal HTML (sha256 pinned above) plus one GET of its print/PDF render (cross_check below). The table was extracted PROGRAMMATICALLY from the raw HTML bytes (the field--name-body container) and compared cell-by-cell, including every footnote marker, against the text drawn in the PDF: all 26 rows agree. It has NOT been re-verified by a second human reviewer, so raw_html_verified stays false and extraction_status stays extracted_draft. Which row governs a given zoning lot, the footnote-1/2/3 street-width and program conditions, and every interaction with Sections 23-433 through 23-436, 23-44 and any commercial overlay or special district MUST be confirmed by a qualified zoning professional (G6) before any rule citing this snapshot is published or Verified.

cross_check.method: The PDF content streams were decompressed and the positioned text of every table cell (district labels with their superscript footnote markers, and the five height values per row) was compared programmatically with the HTML table. verbatim_excerpt:
23-432 Height and setback requirements

R6 R7 R8 R9 R10 R11 R12

In the districts indicated, the minimum base height, maximum base height, and maximum #building# height shall be as set forth in the following table. Separate maximum base heights and maximum #building# heights are set forth for #zoning lots# containing standard #residences# and #zoning lots# containing #qualifying affordable housing# or #qualifying senior housing#.

For portions of a #building# #street wall# that exceed the maximum base height, a setback shall be provided at a height not lower than the minimum base height or higher than the maximum base height in accordance with Section 23-433.

MINIMUM BASE HEIGHT, MAXIMUM BASE HEIGHT,
AND MAXIMUM BUILDING HEIGHTS

[table - see structured `table` field]

1 For #zoning lots# or portions thereof within 100 feet of a #wide street#

2 For #zoning lots# or portions thereof on a #narrow street# beyond 100 feet of a #wide street# or, for #zoning lots# with only #wide street# frontage, portions of such #zoning lot# beyond 100 feet of the #street line#

3 Outside of #Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas#, for #zoning lots#, or portions thereof, located within 100 feet of a #wide street#, containing #UAP developments# or #qualifying senior housing#
verbatim_excerpt_composition:
Verbatim paragraphs of the section body joined by blank lines, in page order: [0] the section number and title as displayed; [1] the district list; [2]-[3] the two operative paragraphs; [4] the table caption (its
kept as a line break); [5] a placeholder for the table, which is carried cell-for-cell in the structured `table` field; [6]-[8] the three table footnotes. Defined terms (bold italic in the HTML) are written #term#, exactly as the portal's print/PDF render writes them. Trailing non-breaking spaces at paragraph ends were dropped and the run of non-breaking spaces after each footnote number was written as one space; no word was changed.

table.caption: MINIMUM BASE HEIGHT, MAXIMUM BASE HEIGHT, AND MAXIMUM BUILDING HEIGHTS
columns: Standard residences - Maximum base height (in feet)
Standard residences - Maximum height of buildings or other structures (in feet)
Qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing - Maximum base height (in feet)
Qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing - Maximum height of buildings or other structures (in feet)
table.header_structure: Two header rows. 'District' and 'Minimum base height (in feet)' each span both header rows (rowspan=2), so the single minimum base height column is not under either program heading. 'Standard #residences#' and '#Qualifying affordable housing# or #qualifying senior housing#' each span two columns (colspan=2): Maximum base height, then Maximum height of #buildings or other structures#.

footnotes.1: For #zoning lots# or portions thereof within 100 feet of a #wide street#
footnotes.2: For #zoning lots# or portions thereof on a #narrow street# beyond 100 feet of a #wide street# or, for #zoning lots# with only #wide street# frontage, portions of such #zoning lot# beyond 100 feet of the #street line#
footnotes.3: Outside of #Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas#, for #zoning lots#, or portions thereof, located within 100 feet of a #wide street#, containing #UAP developments# or #qualifying senior housing#

notes: Captured as the governing-source candidate for the R6-R12 height table (ZR 23-432, City of Yes for Housing Opportunity, Last Amended 12/5/2024). Lane A item A-02a encodes ONLY the R6B row; every other row is carried here for the later R6-R12 family work (queue A-11) and is not used by any rule yet.

R6B ROW, VERIFIED AT THE BYTE LEVEL in both channels: the district cell is a plain 'R6B' (followed by a non-breaking space) with NO <sup> footnote marker, and no value in the row carries a marker. Values: minimum base height 30; standard residences maximum base height 45 and maximum height 55; qualifying affordable or qualifying senior housing maximum base height 45 and maximum height 65. Because no footnote applies, the R6B heights in this table do not depend on street width.

FOOTNOTE PLACEMENT is recorded per row in `district_footnotes`, read from the <sup> markup of each district label and confirmed by the superscripts drawn in the PDF; a row without `district_footnotes` carries no marker on any district or value. Districts that appear in more than one row are NOT a flat lookup - which row governs depends on the footnote condition (street width / Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area / program): R6, R7-1, R7-2, R8, R9, R9A, R9X, R10X, R10, R10A, R11A.
The table's single 'Minimum base height' column applies to the whole row; it is not repeated under the qualifying-housing heading.

Operative text: a setback is required for street-wall portions above the maximum base height, at a height between the minimum and maximum base height, 'in accordance with Section 23-433'. Section 23-433 is NOT captured here; setback depth and any sky-exposure alternative are separate provisions.

Sibling section titles visible in the captured page's navigation (titles only; their text was NOT captured and nothing here relies on it): 23-431 Street wall location requirements; 23-433 Standard setback regulations; 23-434 Height and setback modifications for eligible sites; 23-435 Tower regulations; 23-436 Additional height and setback provisions; 23-44 Special Provisions for Certain Areas (23-441, 23-442, 23-443).
'Qualifying affordable housing' and 'qualifying senior housing' are defined terms; whether a development qualifies is a separate legal determination NOT decided by this snapshot or by any agent.
Nothing in this record is a Verified zoning determination. Verified requires a published rule with G6 qualified-human legal approval.
